title: Scam Calls
about: Hang up on a caller who wants a code, money or a secret.

cards.situation: Sam's phone rings. A calm voice says, "Your Bank fraud team."

image.alt: Sam beside a phone with an incoming call: a grey silhouette, Unknown number, mobile. At the bottom, a red Decline button and a green Accept button with a soft pulse ring.

cards.prompt: Listen to the caller. **Tap each line** to look closer.

parts.job: Anyone can say they're Your Bank, and even a voice can be copied. Neither proves who's calling.
A scare to make you hurry. That's rushing you.
A code arrives when someone types your password. Your Bank never asks for it.
Gift cards are a scammer's favourite: once you send the codes, the money is gone.
"Tell no one" stops anyone helping you check.

cards.explanation: A code, gift cards and "tell no one": this call is a scam.

cards.prompt: Sam reads the texted code out to the caller. **What can they do now?**

image.alt: Sam's phone shows a text: Your Bank code: 482 913. Never share this code. Sam reads it out: 4, 8, 2. Below, three choices: the caller signs in as Sam; stops the payment; nothing, a code alone is useless.
image.revealAlt: The caller's laptop now says Hi, Sam: they're signed in to Sam's account. Sam's phone shows: New sign-in on another device.

options.text: Nothing: a code alone is useless

cards.explanation: The code was the last step of signing in, so reading it out lets the caller in.

cards.title: Hang up, call back
cards.body: If a caller wants a code, money or for you to tell no one, it's a **scam**: hang up. Then call back on a number you already have, like the one on the back of your card.

image.alt: The same call, labelled. Card used now: rushing you. Read me the code: asks for secrets. Buy gift cards: asks for money. Don't tell anyone: tell no one. Below, the red End call button with a cyan ring, Hang up, and the back of a bank card with an arrow: call back here.

cards.prompt: Which calls mean hang up? **Sort each one.**

items.label: "Pay in gift cards, or lose it all."
You ring the number on your card

cards.explanation: Codes, gift cards and "tell no one" mean hang up; a number you chose is fine.
cards.nudge: Check each one: does it want a code, money, or for you to tell no one?
cards.showAnswer: Hang up on the code, the gift cards and "don't tell". Ringing your card's number and a homework call are fine.

cards.prompt: An unknown number rings. It sounds just like Sam's cousin Jess. **Tap what Sam should do.**

image.alt: A call from an unknown number, in a voice like Jess's: Sam, it's Jess! I'm in trouble. Buy gift cards and send me the codes. Tell no one! Below, three choices: buy the gift cards; keep it secret; hang up and call Jess's saved number.
image.revealAlt: Sam hangs up and calls Jess's saved number. The real Jess answers: What? I'm at netball. That wasn't me!

options.nudge: Forget the voice. Which warning signs did you hear?

options.text: Keep it secret, like Jess asked
options.nudge: Forget the voice. Which warning signs did you hear?

options.text: Hang up and call Jess's saved number

cards.explanation: Voices can be copied, but Jess's saved number reaches the real Jess.
cards.showAnswer: Hang up and call Jess's saved number: gift cards and "tell no one" are warning signs, whoever's voice it is.

cards.prompt: "Your Bank" just rang about your card. **Tap the number you'd call back.**

image.alt: Three numbers to call back: a sticky note with the number the caller gave; the phone's recent calls with a Call back button for the last caller; the back of your bank card, with Your Bank's printed number.

options.nudge: Which of these numbers did you already have before the phone rang?
Which of these numbers did you already have before the phone rang?

options.text: The number on the back of your card

cards.explanation: The card's number was there before the call, so the caller can't have chosen it.
cards.showAnswer: The back of your card. The caller chose the other two, so they can lead straight back to the scammer.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
A caller wants a code, money or for you to tell no one? Hang up and call back on a number you already have.

**Try this:** Save your bank's real number (from the back of your card or its own app) in your contacts.

**Next:** A website that looks exactly like your bank's, but isn't.
